insights.summary: Q2 FY27 revenue was a record ₹1,546 Cr (up 35%) with EBITDA of ₹356 Cr (23.0%, down 2.3 points) and PAT of ₹223 Cr. BEV revenue grew 129% and crossed half of automotive revenue; traction motors grew about 50% on the quarter, which diluted margin along with West Asia-driven inflation. Net order book is ₹25,100 Cr after ₹3,600 Cr of new wins, free cash flow in H1 was ₹446 Cr and management keeps the 23-25% margin range and the 10x-in-10-years ambition.

what_changed.text: EBITDA margin range 23-25% kept despite two quarters at about 23%
Priority widened from electrification to 'EPIC' mobility (electric, personalised, intelligent, connected)
Denso JV1 carve-out targeted by end of December; JV2 by H1 CY2027
Deming Prize for the driveline division; three new products commercialised in one quarter

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: There are times when everything comes together in perfect synchronicity, this was that quarter.

analyst_questions.answer: No reason to change the 23-25% range; mix and material prices decide; margin holds if material prices are flat.
Wallet share gains and market growth, including three-wheelers.
Selective M&A (three in a decade) and capex including JV2; a substantial cash balance expected at year-end.

red_flags.text: EBITDA margin fell 2.3 points year on year on mix and inflation; freight nearly doubled in a quarter.
US EV deliveries are flat and the order book is concentrated in a few large customers.
Denso JV economics and timing remain unclear.

watch_next: EBITDA margin staying at or above 23%

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Differential assemblies and gears, EV traction and suspension motors, motor controllers, sensors and railway products
business_snapshot.customers: Global EV and automotive OEMs, Indian two- and three-wheeler makers, railways; 75 EPIC programmes across 37 customers
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: BEV 51% of Q2 automotive revenue (48% in H1)
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: EV adoption, robotics and physical AI orders (about 4% of the order book), railways
